name: GO Classes CS Test Series 2026 | Discrete Mathematics | Topic Wise Test 3

question.text:
Let $\text{S}$ be the set of all functions $f : \text{R} \rightarrow \text{R}.$ Consider the two binary operations $+$ and $\ast$ on $\text{S}$ defined as pointwise addition and composition of functions, as follows.

  • $(f + g)(x) = f (x) + g(x)$
  • $(f \ast g)(x) = f (g(x))$

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\ast$ is commutative.
  2. $+$ and $\ast$ satisfy the left distributive law i.e. $f \ast (g + h) = (f \ast g) + (f \ast h).$
  3. $+$ and $\ast$ satisfy the right distributive law i.e. $(g + h)\ast f = (g \ast f)+ (h \ast f).$

 

  1. All
  2. II only
  3. Ill only
  4. II and III only
Which of the following multiplication tables defined on the set $G = \{a, b, c, d\}$ form a group?

Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be set of integers, and “$+$” be an integer addition operation.

Let $p, q$ be distinct primes. If $\text{J}$ is a proper subgroup of $(\mathbf{Z}, +)$ containing exactly three of $\{p, p + q, pq, p^q, q^p\},$

(Note $:\text{J}$ may contain other elements of $\mathbf{Z}$ which are not in this set), which three elements does $\text{J}$ include?

  1. $\{p, p + q, pq\}$
  2. $\{pq, p^{q}, q^{p}\}$
  3. $\{p, pq, p^{q}\}$
  4. $\{p, pq, q^{p}\}$

Let $G$ be a group under binary operation $\ast.$ Let $g \in G$.

We define $\langle g\rangle$ as follows :
$$\langle g\rangle=\left\{g^{n} \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}\right\}$$

Which of the following is /are true about $\langle g\rangle$ under binary operation $\ast ?$

  1. $\langle g\rangle$ is also a group.
  2. $\langle g\rangle$ is a cyclic subgroup of $G$.
  3. $\langle g\rangle$ is abelian.
  4. If $H \leq G$ and $g \in H$, then $\langle  g\rangle \leq H$.
Let $\text{G}$ be a cyclic group with generator ‘$a$’. Order of ‘$a$’ is $29.$ The number of subgroups $\text{G}$ has ________

The multiplication table $\left({ }^*\right)$ for a group $\mathrm{G}=\{\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{d})$ is given below.
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \ast & a & b & c & d \\
\hline a & a & b & c & d \\
\hline b & b & a & & \\
\hline c & c & & a & \\
\hline d & & & & a \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
Fill in the rest of the table.

Which of the following is/are false?

  1. $d \ast b=d$
  2. $b \ast c=d$
  3. $\left(c\ast d\right) \ast c=d$
  4. $G$ is a cyclic group.

Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be the group of all integers under the operation of addition. Which of the following subsets of $\mathbf{Z}$ is/are NOT a subgroup of $\mathbf{Z}?$

  1. $\{0\}$
  2. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n > 0\}$
  3. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n\;\text{is an even integer}\}$
  4. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n \;\text{is divisible by both 6 and 9}\}$

In a group $\text{G},$ every element other than the identity element has order $2$ then $\mathrm{G}$ is?

  1. Abelian group
  2. Cyclic group
  3. Non-abelian group
  4. Non-cyclic group

Let $\text{R}$ be the set of all real numbers.

Let $\text{S = R} \backslash\{-1\}$ and define a binary operation on $\text{S}$ by $a \ast b=a+b+a b$.

Which of the following is true?

  1. $(\mathrm{S}, \ast)$ is a not a group.
  2. $(\mathrm{S}, \ast)$ is a group but not abelian.
  3. $(\mathrm{S}, \ast)$ is a cyclic group.
  4. $(\mathrm{S}, \ast)$ is an abelian group but not cyclic.

A binary operation “$\ast$” on a set $\text{A}$ is a function from $\text{A} \times \text{A}$ to $\text{A},$ which maps pair $(a, b)$ to $a \ast b.$

Binary operation “$\ast$” on a set $\text{A}$ is commutative if $a \ast b = b \ast a, \forall a, b \in \text{A}.$

The total number of different commutative binary operations on a set of four elements is?
What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that there is a group of order $n$ which is not abelian?

Consider the following statements :

  1. Suppose $\text{G}$ is a group and $a,x \in \text{G}.$ If order of $x=2,$ Then $(a x a^{-1})$ has order $2.$
  2. A finite group is never the union of two of its proper subgroups.

Which of the above statements is/are true?

  1. Only $1$
  2. Only $2$
  3. Both
  4. None

Let $\text{G}_{1}$ and $\text{G}_{2}$ be two groups as following:

  1. $G_1$ is a group such that $\forall x, y, z \in \text{G}_{1}$

          $xy = zx$ implies $y = z$

  1. $\text{G}_{2}$ is a group such that $\forall x, y, z \in \text{G}_{2}$

          $xyz = ayc$ implies $xz = ac$

where $x, y, z, a, c \in \text{G}_{2}$

Then which of the following is True ?

  1. $\text{G}_{1}$ is abelian, $\text{G}_{2}$ is not abelian.
  2. Both $\text{G}_{1}$ and $\text{G}_{2}$ are abelian.
  3. $\text{G}_{2}$ is abelian, not $\text{G}_{1}$.
  4. Neither of $\text{G}_{1}$ and $\text{G}_{2}$ is abelian.
What is the order of smallest non-cyclic group?

Let $\text{G}$ be a group and let $\text{H} = \{x^{–1} | x \in \text{G}\}$ then which of the following is true?

  1. $\text{G} \subseteq \text{H}$ but $\text{G}$ may not be same as $H$
  2. $\text{H} \subseteq \text{G}$ but $\text{H}$ may not be same as $\text{G}$
  3. $\text{H = G}$
  4. $\text{H}$ may not be a group.
